newsitem.title: DENMARK: SOCCER-DENMARK OUTCLASS SLOVENIA TO ROMP HOME 4-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DENMARK OUTCLASS SLOVENIA TO ROMP HOME 4-0.

text.p: Denmark overcame the loss through injury of captain Michael Laudrup to beat Slovenia 4-0 in their World Cup European group one qualifier on Wednesday.

Living up to pre-match promises to take control from the start, the Danes went straight on the offensive and midfielder Allan Nielsen scored the first after just four minutes from a cross by Per Pedersen.
The Danes relentlessly kept probing for openings and in the 28th minute Jan Heintze weaved through the Slovenian defence and lobbed a high ball across the goalmouth where Pedersen headed home.
Slovenia fought back hard but were no match for the Danish teamwork or for Denmark's star goalkeeper Peter Schmiechel.
Slovenian coach Zbenko Verdenik acknowledged that his players were outclassed all the way.
"Denmark played very, very well, they were two classes above the Slovenians. Denmark has showed what modern football is about," he told reporters after the game.

The Danes kept up the pressure in the second half, coming close several times before Brian Laudrup shot his team's third goal straight past Slovenian goalkeeper Bosko Boskovic in the 52nd minute from a penalty after a failed attempt by Nielsen.
Nielsen grabbed his second four minutes later, receiving a head shot from Marc Rieper, to make it 4-0 and leave Denmark nicely placed on 10 points with three wins and a draw.
Danish coach Bo Johanssen was pleased with his team's performance but warned that the road ahead to next year's finals in France was long and hard.
"It was a good match. Denmark played very well and I hope that they will show that again in the next matches, but we must not imagine that we can win the coming matches as easily," he said.
Scorer Alan Pedersen was asked how he had the confidence to play such an agressive game when he is yet to graduate from the reserve bench at his British league side, Blackburn Rovers.
"Our coach had confidence in me and I couldn't let him down," he said.
